posts.body:
Poseidon Aerospace just closed a **$60M Series A** ahead of the first test flight of *Egret*, its uncrewed cargo plane, [per TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/08/poseidon-aerospace-lands-60m-ahead-of-first-pilotless-test-flight/). The thesis is refreshingly un-flashy: no VTOL, no hydrogen, no electric powertrain — just fixed wings, combustion engines, and pilots removed from the cost equation. As CEO David Zagaynov put it, "It's really hard to beat the energy density of fuels of anything carbon-related."

For traders, this is a clean binary to price. **Will Egret complete its first pilotless flight by year-end 2026?** That's a resolvable, on-chain-friendly question — exactly the kind of milestone-driven event EventTrader markets are built for. Autonomy-in-logistics is a multi-year narrative, and each funding round, test flight, and regulatory nod becomes a tradeable catalyst.

The deeper play is the aerologistics cost-curve story: capital is flowing toward companies attacking unit economics rather than chasing spectacle. Build your book around the catalysts — the maiden flight, the FAA posture, the first paying cargo route — and let the market do the pricing.
posts.title: Poseidon Aerospace's $60M Bet on Boring: A Prediction Market Playbook
